title: ChipBlocks provenance fragment
description: Shared 'value with provenance' schema fragment per ADR-007. Used by material properties (materials.yaml), device parameters (devices.yaml), and Active Variables (parameters.yaml). The same fragment shape applies everywhere a value with empirical or sourced basis lives in the system. Other schemas reference this via $ref. Required-vs-optional fields differ per origin (builtin / community / user-local / project); see ADR-007 for the full origin matrix.

value.description: The actual value. May be a number (most common), a string (for enums or labels), or a boolean (for feature-flag-style values).

units.description: SI unit string when the value is a quantity. Examples: 'V', 'A', 'ohm', 'ohm_meter', 'F', 'H', 'K', 'degC', 'N', 'W', 'W_per_mK', 'kg_per_m3', 'Hz', 'm', 'mm', 'um', 'V_per_m'. Omit for non-quantity values (strings, booleans). Conditions/tolerance use the same unit string format.

type.description: Kind of source, ordered roughly by trustworthiness: standard (NIST/IEC/IEEE/ISO/JEDEC/IPC) > reference (textbook, handbook) > datasheet (manufacturer) > pdk (process design kit doc) > community (curated wiki / fab design rules) > measured (user empirical) > estimated (user guess) > user_supplied (user typed it).

label.description: Human-readable description of where this value comes from. Examples: 'Copper resistivity at 20 C', '9V alkaline battery nominal voltage'.

citation.description: URL, standards reference, datasheet citation, or measurement record. Required for builtin + community origins when source.type != user_supplied. Examples: 'NIST CODATA 2018', 'IEC 60721-3-3 Class 3K3', 'TI LM7805 datasheet rev. 2024', 'JLCPCB capability matrix 2026-01-15'.

conditions.description: Implicit assumptions baked into the value. Map of named condition (temperature, pressure, forward_current, state_of_charge, etc.) to { value, units } or a string label (e.g., 'full' for state_of_charge). The validator may use these to warn when the design operates outside documented conditions. STRONGLY ENCOURAGED for shipped values; optional for user-supplied.

confidence.description: How trustworthy the value is at the documented conditions. high = well-defined constant / standards-based / precisely-measured (±5% under stated conditions). medium = typical datasheet value or measurement with limited validation (±10-30%). low = estimate or limited-info value. unknown = not assessed (default for user-added).

tolerance.description: The actual range under stated conditions. Distinct from confidence: a high-confidence value can still have wide tolerance (e.g., a 5% resistor is precisely ±5%). Optional; omit when not meaningful.

notes.description: Freeform caveats, edge cases, or recommendations the user should know about.
